title: KV-ensemble preemptive fairness (KEPF) — staged soft-preemptor for continuous batching
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Context: Continuous batching is our primary path to high throughput, but preemption events (forced interrupts to meet higher-priority latency SLOs) currently cause KV cache churn and GPU memory fragmentation, driving up token cost and SLO violations for tail tenants. This ticket defines and implements a staged, tenant-weighted soft-preemption policy (KEPF) that reduces KV thrash and preserves hotset residency while still honoring strict latency SLOs. The design intentionally separates preemption decisioning into two cooperating mechanisms: a fast probabilistic soft-preemptor (in-path) for immediate admission decisions, and an asynchronous eviction coordinator (background) that performs graceful KV reshaping, snapshotting, and compaction hooks before hard evictions occur.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end implementation behind feature flag that can be toggled at route level
Simulator results: 30%+ reduction in SLO violations at p95 for multi-tenant pathological workloads compared to baseline preemptor
KV miss rate reduced for hot tenants by >=20% during sustained preemption windows
No user-facing increase in median latency outside canary cluster; CPU overhead <= 7% on serving nodes
Runbook and canary dashboard added to Console; automatic rollback if preemption-induced error rate increases >3x
benchmark_results: Simulated 100-tenant mix w/ 10% tail-heavy load: baseline p95 SLO breaches = 12.4% -> KEPF = 8.1% (35% relative improvement)
KV hotset retention: baseline eviction rate during preempt cycles = 18% -> KEPF soft-reserve eviction = 5%
GPU memory fragmentation metric (compaction score): improved by 22% in flagged hosts when compaction hook enabled
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged rollout to canary pool (10 nodes) with traffic mirroring and shadow mode for 72 hours
Promote to regional canaries (2 regions) after success criteria; enable route-level opt-in for customers with high SLO sensitivity
Monitor p50/p95/p99 latencies, KV hit rate, GPU compaction score, and CPU overhead; extend canary if any metric regresses >5%
Full cluster rollout conditional on 2-week stability and signoff from SRE and Runtime teams
tradeoffs: Pros: preserves hot KV residency, fewer tail SLO breaches, smoother memory utilization, controlled hard-evictions
Cons: adds meta-state for staged snapshots (small memory overhead), increases CPU for eviction coordinator, more complex tracing for debugging
Operational: some tenants may see slower eviction of cold entries, slightly elevated memory pressure during snapshot window
tasks: Design API for route-level preemption policy flags (PM/Console)
Implement in-path probabilistic soft-preemptor (runtime) with tenant-weighted scoring
Eviction coordinator: implement snapshot/compact/commit flow and GPU compaction hook
Add telemetry: new metrics (preempt_decision, soft_preempt_rate, staged_snapshot_size, kv_hot_retention)
E2E tests: multi-tenant regression, fragmentation stress, and SLO injection tests
Console: dashboard and canary alerting integration
Prepare runbook and automated rollback policy
